wi-coverage.description: Coverage contract: population, checked, notChecked, and notApplicable are the partition buckets; residue is a separate list, never a fifth bucket. Every population entry must appear verbatim in exactly one status bucket. All buckets are string arrays; an explicit empty residue array (residue:[]) declares zero residue, and residue:['none'] remains accepted as a compatibility form. Universal-verification closes must include the residue array. Omitted status buckets mean empty buckets.

population.description: The complete, uniquely named population. Copy each entry verbatim into exactly one status bucket.

checked.description: Population entries verified as checked; entries must be copied verbatim and appear at most once.

notChecked.description: Population entries not verified; entries must be copied verbatim and appear at most once.

notApplicable.description: Population entries that do not apply; entries must be copied verbatim and appear at most once.

residue.description: A separate residue list, never a partition bucket; for universal closes it must be present and may be empty. Use [] or ['none'] for zero residue.

classRef.description: Derived from each persisted subject plan class when omitted; explicit values must match. Ad-hoc scopes require an explicit class attestation.

evidenceRefs.description: Exact immutable evidence identities to grade. Use this to exclude superseded run-specific bindings without deleting history; include every relied-on ref across the enforced clauses.

current.description: Current fingerprints for the exact bound evidence refs. `specAdequacy.current` entries use `{ planSlug?, specId?, specRevision?, specFingerprint?, evidenceKind, evidenceRef, sourceFingerprint, testFingerprint?, fixtureFingerprint?, rubricFingerprint?, environmentFingerprint? }`; provide one entry for every selected bound evidence ref (`specAdequacy.evidenceRefs` narrows the selection; when omitted, use all bound refs) and every stored fingerprint dimension. `planSlug`, `specId`, `specRevision`, and `specFingerprint` are an all-or-none clause identity; omitted values remain unknown and cannot pass.

wi-adequacy.description: Required on a terminal close that covers active test-requiring spec clauses. The gate recomputes per-clause adequacy over the optional exact evidenceRefs selection and accepts only exact current terminal scorecards whose grading audit is settled. A single-clause replay supplies specRevision + specFingerprint; a multi-clause replay supplies full clause identity on every current[] row with replaySnapshot:true.

wi-assumptions.description: Required for a terminal close; omit for record-only completions. Pass "none" or fact keys.

fullDefinitions.name: work_items__create
fullDefinitions.description: Create ONE or MANY work-items. bug/change/task file tracked issues; feature enters the harness queue; chunk is retired (rejected). If creation requests an assignment to a fleet MEMBER outside that member's claim scope, the finding is retained as an explicitly unassigned, claim-held filing with a visible downgrade — it never grants an out-of-scope claim. Single: { kind, title, … }; many: items:[…]. Returns per-item outcomes, including a visible warning when dedup coverage is degraded.

harness.description: harness slug — required for feature; sets scope for bug/change. Also the DEFAULT harness for items that omit one.

cadence.description: explicit cadence for routing_intent=schedule-recurrence, e.g. "daily at 09:00" or a cron expression

urgent.description: URGENT enqueue: wake the brain immediately (floor-debounced). Reserve for a production fire, not routine filing.

force.description: Override the dupe guards (EI-316 mirror, semantic cosine, exact identity).

assign_to.description: Atomically CLAIM the new item for this agent id in the SAME create (B-LOOP-4) — pass a concrete ownerId, or the literal "self" to resolve to the caller. Omit ⇒ unclaimed.

items.description: create many work-items at once — each is a full create spec.

harness.description: harness slug — required for feature/chunk; sets scope for bug/change. Falls back to the batch `harness` default.

parent.description: parent work-item id (feature-family; required-shape for a chunk)

cadence.description: explicit cadence for routing_intent=schedule-recurrence, e.g. "daily at 09:00" or a cron expression

urgent.description: URGENT enqueue: wake the brain immediately (floor-debounced). Reserve for a production fire.

force.description: Override the dupe guards (EI-316 mirror, semantic cosine, exact identity) for this item.

assign_to.description: Atomically CLAIM this item for this agent id in the SAME create (B-LOOP-4) — pass a concrete ownerId, or the literal "self" to resolve to the caller. Overrides assign_all_to_self for this item.

conditionReplay.description: For immutable revision identities: reuse the original conditionKey filing after closure too, without reopening or rewriting its disposition. Requires conditionKey and a concrete workspace. Omit for recurring alarms.

assign_all_to_self.description: Claim every created item for YOU (your ownerId) — unless an item carries its own assign_to.

workspace.description: target workspace id — defaults to the request workspace (MCP ?workspace=). EI-728 routing for the inline create / every item.

phone_producer.description: Admit a Phone voice producer from the configured authenticated host. Room selector only; host records supply identity and canonical binding. Exclusive with ordinary create metadata.

0.description: Plan item this work-item IMPLEMENTS ({ slug, item:"P-003" }): writes a work→plan_item coverage edge so it rolls up into that item; completing the item can auto-resolve it as residue. A bug merely DISCOVERED while working an item is NOT implementing it — file it unlinked (EI-19460536530145188).

1.description: The kind(s) of change this work makes, from the bundled catalog: ui, service, migration, background-job, logic, docs, config, test-only, no-code-change. A successful close must carry each kind's proof. Re-declaring later keeps the earlier declaration in history.

2.description: initial lifecycle state (EI-10897) — e.g. 'wip' to open an ad-hoc unit you are starting RIGHT NOW (pair with assign_to:'self'). Defaults to the kind's normal entry state (todo). Terminal states and 'blocked' are rejected: complete the item instead, or create it then name its blocker with work_items:set_blocker.

3.description: owner-directive provenance: the orders id this work-item is being created to carry out (harness_shared.owner_directives.id). Late-binding and one-directional — the directive is never written back. Omit for ordinary work; a directive with zero linked work-items is healthy, not degenerate.

4.description: Pot to scope this to (the pot home-harness slug). Omit in a harness-scoped session — it auto-resolves from your harness (a member harness resolves to its pot's home). A workspace-spanning caller (Mug/overwatch) that can't auto-resolve must pass an explicit pot.

5.description: inline typed links (WI-3956) written from the new item to targets on create — e.g. [{ rel:"investigates", target_id:"EI-9250" }]. Best-effort: a bad target is skipped, never fails the create.

6.description: recurring-detector filing identity (WI-39604): an OPEN item already holding this key is refreshed and returned (see conditionUpsert on the result) instead of a sibling being filed — single-host system filers only.

7.description: explicit papercusp-way routing intent. Body/summary prose is never classified. schedule-recurrence also requires cadence.

8.description: built-in kind (feature, bug, change, task); 'chunk' is deprecated (historical rows remain readable) OR a workspace-registered generic-kind datatype (declared via meta:define-datatype)

9.description: alias for `summary` — the item body text (work_items:update names it `body`). Pass either; both-with-different-values is rejected (WI-4492).

rel.description: the relationship: blocks | relates | duplicates | fixes | investigates | about | caused-by | revises

target_kind.description: explicit coord ObjectRef kind (e.g. plan_item, event) — use with target_ref

target_ref.description: explicit coord ObjectRef ref — use with target_kind

satisfaction.description: blocks-only outcome requirement; omitted defaults to settled

a.description: Why the declared kinds changed or were first declared late. Stored with the declaration.

fullDefinitions.name: work_items__get
fullDefinitions.description: Read work-items by ID (`id` for one; `ids` for a batch). Returns `{ ok, results:[…], counts }`; correlate rows by id, not position. Batch reads also include a per-requested-ID receipt. Read `returns` for conditional warnings.

id.description: a single work-item id (n=1 shorthand for ids:[id])

attachments.description: Standalone one-item consented attachment read: {} lists metadata; id returns a base64 byte page (default 1024 bytes, max 2048). Canonical fixes resolve original report evidence. Expired evidence is unavailable.

ids.description: work-item ids for ordinary reads (1–100). With resume:true, provide one ID only; prefer the id argument for a continuation read.

harness.description: caller harness scope; do not copy a cross-hive row's canonical harness here

detail.description: also return topics, thread posts (comments), outgoing links, `lifecycle` — the unified history (blocks, holds, reopens) with a coverage report saying what is NOT recorded — and `priorAttempts`, the bounded prior-attempt brief (what was already tried on this item's plan lane, and what the budget OMITTED). Accepts `true`/`false`, or the aliases `'full'`/`'summary'` (some tools in this catalog use that string-enum convention instead).

checksOnly.description: return only the stored checkpoint check-row ledger (`checkpointChecks.rows` with caller-facing id/claim identities) plus recency/failure metadata; omit the checkpoint narrative and other enrichments. Use this before building `retireIds` instead of fetching the full checkpoint body.

checkpointOnly.description: standalone exact checkpoint text page for exactly one item; skips item payload and other enrichments. Pair with root-level offset (Unicode code points, default 0) and limit (default 512, hard cap 768); follow checkpointPage.nextOffset and compare checkpointContentHash across pages. checkpointPage:null means no stored checkpoint unless checkpointReadFailed is true.

offset.description: checkpointOnly page start measured in Unicode code points; omitted means 0. The returned checkpointPage.offset is clamped to totalChars.

limit.description: checkpointOnly page size in Unicode code points; omitted means 512. Larger requests are clamped to 768 and disclosed in checkpointPage.limitClamped.

resume.description: Standalone one-item continuation view: current claim, complete structured next action, saved checks and exact evidence references, with freshness and scoped recovery. Pass exactly one item (prefer id; a one-element ids array is accepted, but multi-id batches are rejected). Uses checkpoint:{did,left,next} written by work_items:checkpoint; missing/unreadable state remains explicit. Checks are at results[].resume.checks.rows (an array), not resume.checks; resume.checks.omitted counts saved rows excluded by the packet budget. Do not combine with detail, checksOnly, checkpointOnly, offset, limit, threadLimit, priorAttemptRefs, or operationalBrief; use a separate read for those enrichments.

operationalBrief.description: Add `operationalBrief` per row: claim/state, blockers, last verified evidence, next action and successor residue, projected from this same read. Unmeasured fields are explicit `unknown` with a reason, never zero. Forces a complete read; not with resume or checksOnly.

priorAttemptRefs.description: raw drill-down for the requested work-item(s): pass `id` (one) or `ids` (many) together with these refs. Resolve refs back to their FULL untruncated source records. When combined with `detail:true`, this replaces the bounded `priorAttempts` brief so the response does not mix clipped history with the raw records; make a separate read if you need both views. Take refs from a brief's `omission.omittedRefs` (records the budget could only COUNT) or from a clipped record's own `rawRef` — the brief names them precisely so a bounded read is never a dead end. Refs that no longer resolve come back in `unresolved[]`, which is an answer about the history, not an error.

threadLimit.description: return a bounded oldest-first recent-comment window instead of loading the full thread; 0 explicitly suppresses thread work, positive values return up to 10 posts with a same-snapshot total. The effective window is capped at 10: a larger value is CLAMPED (not rejected) and the result reports `threadLimitClamped:{requested,applied}` — read `threadWindow.total`, not `shown`, for how many posts exist.

parameters.x-papercusp-call-constraint: resume requires one item (pass `id`, or a one-element `ids` array; multi-id batches are not supported) and cannot be combined with detail, checksOnly, checkpointOnly, offset, limit, threadLimit, priorAttemptRefs or operationalBrief; use a separate read for those enrichments (two calls: work_items:get { id, resume:true } for the continuation, then work_items:get { id, detail:true } for the detail record)

fullDefinitions.name: work_items__list
fullDefinitions.description: List work-items across kinds (feature/chunk/bug/change/task). Default shows top-level items (chunks are hidden — pass parent or includeChildren). Filter by harness, kind, state, or q (a case-insensitive literal substring over title, body/summary, and retained capture occurrence title/body). Returns the WorkItem array directly — each row's summary is EXCERPTED to keep the list bounded (a row carries summary_truncated + summary_full_chars when cut); use work_items:get { id } for a full body.

prDeliveryAudit.description: Read-only PR-bypass audit of EVERY admission from explicit workflow ruleIds, including disabled rules and rules omitting delivery:pr. Returns {prDeliveryAudit}; missing evidence or truncated populations are unknown. Ordinary list filters do not narrow this audit.

includeBody.description: Internal source projection override: omit issue body/summary when false.

includePayload.description: Internal source projection override: omit JSONB payload when false.

q.description: case-insensitive literal substring matched against title and body/summary

kind.description: built-in kind (feature, chunk, bug, change, task) OR a workspace-registered generic-kind datatype

state.description: WI-38339: ONE state, or an ARRAY of states (matches any of them). Alias: `states` (alias-group:state|states). An empty array is NO filter, never 'match nothing'. For the dominant question — everything still open — prefer `notTerminal`, which cannot drift as the terminal spellings change.

states.description: Alias for the ARRAY form of `state` (alias-group:state|states) — matches any supplied state. Passing both names is rejected unless the caller uses only one spelling.

notTerminal.description: WI-38339: exclude every state terminal in EITHER family (done/passed/resolved/closed/deprecated/dropped), derived from the canonical union rather than a copied list. The 'everything not finished' filter agents otherwise hand-write as `status NOT IN (…)` in raw SQL.

createdSince.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone — rows created at or after it (INCLUSIVE, like plans:list).

updatedSince.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone — rows updated at or after it (INCLUSIVE, like plans:list).

sourcePlanSlug.description: Persisted item provenance only: rows produced or stamped by this plan. It does NOT include ad-hoc work merely performed while a session/fleet declared that plan; scheduler `plan` predicates are item-provenance filters too. Alias: `plan` (alias-group:sourcePlanSlug|plan).

plan.description: Alias for `sourcePlanSlug` (alias-group:sourcePlanSlug|plan) — the SAME item-provenance filter. Passing both with different values is rejected.

assignee.description: Filter to items assigned to this agent (feature → taken_by; issue → assignee). The literal "self" resolves to YOU (as it does in work_items:claim / claim_next / create's assign_to); `mine: true` is the same request.

assignedBy.description: Filter issue-family items by the owner who delegated them (the durable `assigned_by` field). This filter is ignored for feature-family rows, which have no delegator column.

mine.description: Filter to items assigned to the CALLER (resolves your own agent identity) — EI-6506: a leader's 'see your work item' handoff, findable without raw PG or knowing your own ownerId string. Overridden by an explicit `assignee` if both are passed.

parent.description: list children (chunks) of this parent id

includeChildren.description: include child items (chunks) in the list

admissibleOnly.description: EI-7841/WI-3649: a cheap pre-filter, NOT the full claim-floor verdict. Feature-family: the G2 admission/trust gate (remote, un-admitted, untrusted-author) work_items:claim/claim_next enforce. Issue-family (bug/change/task): every ROW-INTRINSIC claim floor — remote origin, observation lane, replication-liveness detector, claim-hold, needs-human, reserved-plan-lane, loop-noise, already-terminally-completed, active external blocker (WI-4405/WI-37761/WI-37774). It does NOT apply the floors needing live claim context (blocked-dep / cooldown / rig / swarm-affinity / redundancy), so a row it admits may STILL be unclaimable — the origin+lane-only version caused the 2026-07-12 idle-fleet miss. ⚠ NOT the claimable verdict: for 'what issue-family work can I claim right now' use work_items:claimable (the full floors). Default false (full backlog incl. gated items, for overview/leader reads).

audit.description: Integrity diagnostics: terminal rows, except worked-then-abandoned (nonterminal: claimed/worked/released >21d ago). DETECTOR, not verdict: read each row; never bulk-close. work_items:stranded instead examines checkpoints. No-evidence closes now land authority:proposed and stay owned. no-completion-record = missing completionRef and authority, usually legacy/system bypass; suspicious = local rows without recognized system closer, investigate write paths; federated = remote-origin awareness, not proof of a local bypass. geometry-unverified = layout file (*.css/*.tsx/*.jsx) with unit/absent verifiedHow; intermittent-underevidenced = flaky/racy title with only pass streaks, lacking failure rate/root cause/deterministic reproduction; reconciler-sourced = mirrors plan status without independent verification. Newest-first; composes with state.

completionAuthority.description: Filter TERMINAL rows by the completion-authority judgement the P-004 gate stamped: 'committed' (evidence sufficient — verifiedHow PLUS testsRun/testResult), 'proposed' (closed but under-evidenced: recorded, out of burn-down, still owned by its closer), 'validated'/'pending_human'/'invalid', or 'unjudged' for a close carrying NO judgement. This is how you LIST under-evidenced closes — the read D-012 left open when P-006/D-003 deleted the 'no-evidence' audit bucket. ⚠ 'unjudged' measures the INSTRUMENT, not the agents: only work_items:complete stamps an authority, so a close made via the bare state-write path lands NULL however well evidenced it was (that path records its evidence in terminalCompletionRef instead, and complete's structured evidence lands in payload._completionEvidence — three places, so no single field is a complete evidence test). Measured 2026-07-27: 38.2% of that day's agent closes were gate-judged vs 0.1% the day before, so an 'unjudged' hit means "never judged", NOT "unevidenced". Non-terminal rows never match. Composes with `state` and `audit`.

includeObservations.description: EI-10422: by default a payload.lane:'observation' row (a turn-end reflection / rubric scorecard filed via improvements:capture { lane:'observation' }) is EXCLUDED — by design (D-005) it never enters the work queue/triage. Pass true to include raw observations in this read (a curation surface); the default keeps the backlog/triage view free of the ~2,700 open notes that otherwise masquerade as claimable `change` work.

natures.description: P-010/D-011: natures to return (work|record|document|event). Default: work only, unless kind is named. ['record'] reads record rows such as pipeline deals.

audience.description: D-041: 'agent' = only rows an agent may claim/close; 'human' = human-audience rows; 'any' = both. Default for agent callers: 'agent', unless kind or natures is named.

fullDefinitions.name: work_items__release
fullDefinitions.description: Release one OR many work-items (clear assignee / taken_by) so another agent can pick them up. Single: { id }. Many: { ids:[…] } or items:[{ id, harness? }]. `claimHold:true` (both families) ALSO durably parks the item out of claim_next/scheduler:get_next self-select (WI-2797) and requires `claimHoldRelease:{condition,trigger,owner?}`; the writer resolves reachability/evidence from the event ledger. The park survives your session ending, remains claimable by id, and `claimHold:false` clears it.

items.description: release many, each { id, harness?, claimHold? }

harness.description: per-item harness (else the batch `harness` default)

claimHold.description: per-item claim-hold override (else the batch `claimHold` default)

claimHoldRelease.description: typed release condition required when the effective claimHold is true

condition.description: the concrete condition that permits this durable park to be reconsidered

trigger.description: the exact events:await key that signals the condition may have changed

owner.description: accountable condition owner/source; defaults to the parker

force.description: per-item override of the batch `force` default

reason.description: per-item override of the batch `reason` (required when force clears a peer's claim)

harness.description: default harness for the inline id / ids / items that omit one

claimHold.description: default claim-hold for the inline id / every id in `ids` (both families): true excludes the item from claim_next/scheduler:get_next self-select until cleared; false clears a prior hold.

claimHoldRelease.description: default typed release condition for claimHold:true; reachability/evidence are resolved by the writer

condition.description: the concrete condition that permits this durable park to be reconsidered

trigger.description: the exact events:await key that signals the condition may have changed

owner.description: accountable condition owner/source; defaults to the parker

force.description: default force for the inline id / every id in `ids`: release even if held by ANOTHER agent. CHECKED override (WI-4198): allowed only when the holder is not live, or you are queen, or you lead the HOLDER's fleet — and a cross-holder force requires `reason` and is audited + notifies holder/owner. Default false: refuses with { error:"not_holder", holder } when the caller is not the current holder.

reason.description: default reason for the inline id / every id in `ids` — REQUIRED when force clears another agent's claim; auto-truncated to 500 chars if longer, then recorded in the audit row/notifications and any durable park.

parameters.x-papercusp-call-constraint: claimHold:true requires claimHoldRelease { condition, trigger, owner? }; durable parks must declare a typed re-evaluation contract (including per-item overrides and batch defaults)

fullDefinitions.name: work_items__set_state
fullDefinitions.description: Set state for one or many work-items: open|wip|blocked|needs-human|done|dropped (legacy aliases preserve terminal_reason). Terminal writes need completionRef + assumptions ("none" or facts:assert keys). Blocked writes need work_items:set_blocker; use work_items:link { rel:"blocks" } for internal dependencies. Plan-linked features use plans:set-status. Reopen terminal items with force:true. Supports id, ids, or items; inspect expectedState/appliedState. Readback mismatches fail.

harness.description: default harness for items that omit one

reason.description: apply to every row: terminal rows use it as completion evidence, progress rows record it as a comment; blocked rows require a typed blocker and refuse free text

note.description: same as batch `reason` — apply to every eligible row; pass only one

force.description: EI-7422: required to REOPEN an item that already carries a terminal completion (terminalOwner + terminalCompletionRef) — without it the write is REJECTED rather than silently discarding a peer's completion. Only needed when the target is already terminal AND you are deliberately reopening it.

completionRef.description: REQUIRED for this terminal state — completion evidence (summary / commit / coord or plan-item ref). Prefer work_items:complete for a structured completion record.

force.description: EI-7422: required to REOPEN an item that already carries a terminal completion (terminalOwner + terminalCompletionRef) — without it the write is REJECTED rather than silently discarding a peer's completion. Only needed when the target is already terminal AND you are deliberately reopening it.

reason.description: why the item moved — recorded as a comment on the item (a non-terminal state has no reason field of its own)

force.description: EI-7422: required to REOPEN an item that already carries a terminal completion (terminalOwner + terminalCompletionRef) — without it the write is REJECTED rather than silently discarding a peer's completion. Only needed when the target is already terminal AND you are deliberately reopening it.

state.description: Use only after an active typed blocker exists: call work_items:set_blocker for an external blocker or work_items:link { rel:"blocks" } for a work-item dependency. Plan-linked feature items use plans:set-status.

decision.description: P-114 risk/authority for the inline id / every id in `ids`

completionRef.description: completion evidence applied to the inline id / every id in `ids` (see itemSpec.completionRef)

force.description: required to reopen an already-terminally-completed item; only needed for a deliberate reopen

0.description: REQUIRED — the `facts:assert` KEYS this close rests on (e.g. ["gate-red-is-flake-not-regression"]), or the literal "none" if it rests on no recorded assumption. There is deliberately NO default: a terminal close removes the item from the queue, so a wrong assumption leaves with it and nobody can catch it afterwards. Saying "none" is a valid answer; omitting the field is not.

2.description: alias for `completionRef` on a TERMINAL state — refused on a non-terminal one, which persists no reason field

fullDefinitions.name: work_items__update
fullDefinitions.description: Edit one OR many work-items' title/body/severity/kind/found-during/linked feature/parent/goal/plan_item/needsTwoMachineRig/needsHuman; notifies subscribers. Single: { id, …fields }; many: items:[{ id, …fields }]. Returns per-item { ok, id, item? | error }; missing items do not fail the batch. Goal and plan_item are family-agnostic; parent is the duplicate/child relation and null clears it. Other field edits are issue-family-only (bug/change/task); features remain pipeline-owned. Body shrink is rejected unless confirmShrink:true (EI-8497). needsTwoMachineRig toggles payload.needs_2_machine_rig; compatibility input needsHuman:true writes the strict payload.needsOwnerAction gate, while false clears both legacy and strict keys. `payload` shallow-MERGES free-form keys onto an existing item (admission/claim and `_`-prefixed keys refused). (State → work_items:set_state; structural decisions → work_items:amend; tags → work_items:tag; comments → work_items:comment.)

kind.description: correct a mislabeled work-item kind — bug = broken (auto-implement-eligible), change = desired improvement (human-gated)

confirmShrink.description: EI-8497: a `body` edit that would replace a substantial existing body with something far shorter is REJECTED by default (a fat-finger guard — there's no body revision history to recover from a mis-call). Pass true to confirm a genuinely intended drastic shrink.

needsTwoMachineRig.description: WI-2796: mark (true) or unmark (false) this item as requiring a live ≥2-machine / Hetzner federation rig to work — scheduler:get_next / claim_next then exclude it from single-box self-select instead of letting single-box agents claim-then-release it repeatedly (EI-18151406094317010). Sets payload.needs_2_machine_rig.

needsHuman.description: Compatibility input for the owner-action gate: true writes payload.needsOwnerAction=true and removes legacy payload.needsHuman; false unsets BOTH keys and re-admits the row. Reserve true for a genuine credential, physical-device, or external-service action only — product decisions use agent review.

items.description: update many work-items at once — each { id, …fields }. A top-level field (title/body/severity/kind/foundDuring/linkedFeatureId/parent/goal/plan_item/harness) is the DEFAULT applied to every item that omits its own (EI-7639) — pass it once instead of repeating it per item.

harness.description: per-item harness (else the batch `harness` default)

kind.description: correct a mislabeled work-item kind — bug = broken (auto-implement-eligible), change = desired improvement (human-gated)

confirmShrink.description: EI-8497: a `body` edit that would replace a substantial existing body with something far shorter is REJECTED by default (a fat-finger guard — there's no body revision history to recover from a mis-call). Pass true to confirm a genuinely intended drastic shrink.

needsTwoMachineRig.description: WI-2796: mark (true) or unmark (false) this item as requiring a live ≥2-machine / Hetzner federation rig to work — scheduler:get_next / claim_next then exclude it from single-box self-select instead of letting single-box agents claim-then-release it repeatedly (EI-18151406094317010). Sets payload.needs_2_machine_rig.

needsHuman.description: Compatibility input for the owner-action gate: true writes payload.needsOwnerAction=true and removes legacy payload.needsHuman; false unsets BOTH keys and re-admits the row. Reserve true for a genuine credential, physical-device, or external-service action only — product decisions use agent review.

harness.description: default harness for the inline id / items that omit one

0.description: Opted-in frozenTests: pilot only. Register an independently authored manual test-only evidence binding plus red calibration; use alone. Re-freeze requires a named Decision and expectedRevision.

bindingId.description: Independent author's current manual spec binding; measurement sourcePaths and testPaths must be exactly the frozen tests.

decisionId.description: Required for re-freeze: Decision with a frozen-tests JSON fence naming itemId, fromRevision, toRevision, previousBindingId, bindingId and reason.

1.description: plan item this existing work-item implements (for example { slug:"my-plan", item:"P-003" }); stamps payload.plan_item so plan-scoped fleet lanes can admit it and writes the same coverage edge as work_items:create. Pass null to CLEAR the stamp when it asserts something untrue (the item does not implement that plan item) — this removes the payload key and retracts the coverage edge, releasing the item from the plan-item lane-sync hold and the sibling-close machinery.

2.description: MERGE these keys into payload (shallow jsonb merge — sibling keys are preserved, never replaced). For durable per-item metadata a plan or rubric rules must live on the artifact. Admission/claim keys (plan_item, needs_2_machine_rig, needsOwnerAction, needsHuman, lane, claim_hold_*) and `_`-prefixed internal keys are REFUSED — use their dedicated args, which also apply the coverage edge and legacy-key unsets a bare merge would skip.

3.description: Ask the end-user reporter one follow-up question. Only the current fixer may ask; actor/id/time are server-stamped, text is redacted, and retry is idempotent. Use alone, without other edits. The reporter replies from their install.
